hyperedges.label: Always-On Graph Guidance Across Assistant Platforms
Prompt-Injection Defense Chain for the Semantic Pass

nodes.label: Always-On Assistant Install Commands
nodes.rationale: Writes a config file so the assistant consults the knowledge graph for codebase questions, preferring scoped `graphify query` over reading the full report or grepping raw files.

nodes.label: Hook Platforms (Claude Code, Gemini CLI)
nodes.rationale: A PreToolUse hook fires before search-style tool calls and file reads to nudge the assistant toward the graph path instead of grepping.

nodes.label: Instruction-File Platforms (Codex, OpenCode, Cursor)
nodes.rationale: Persistent instruction files such as AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules provide the same query-first guidance where no hook mechanism exists.

nodes.label: graphify codex install
nodes.rationale: The .codex/hooks.json PreToolUse hook is deliberately a no-op because Codex Desktop rejects hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext on PreToolUse, which would break Bash tool calls; AGENTS.md carries the always-on guidance instead.

nodes.label: graphify claude install
nodes.rationale: Installs CLAUDE.md plus a PreToolUse hook (graphify hook-guard) that does the nudging on Claude Code.

nodes.label: graphify codebuddy install
nodes.rationale: Mirrors Claude Code: writes a CODEBUDDY.md section and installs PreToolUse hooks in .codebuddy/settings.json that fire before Bash search commands and file reads.

nodes.label: graphify kilo install
nodes.rationale: Writes a native tool.execute.before plugin plus .kilo config registration so Kilo gets the always-on reminder through native config rather than a generic instruction file.

nodes.label: graphify cursor install
nodes.rationale: Writes .cursor/rules/graphify.mdc with alwaysApply: true so Cursor includes it in every conversation automatically, making a hook unnecessary.

nodes.label: The "Why" — Rationale Nodes
nodes.rationale: Inline comments (NOTE/WHY/HACK), docstrings, and design rationale from docs are extracted as separate nodes linked to the code they explain.

nodes.label: Confidence Tags (EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.rationale: Every inferred relationship is tagged so the user always knows what was found versus guessed.

nodes.label: Local Tree-sitter Code Extraction
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted locally via AST with no API calls so a code-only corpus needs no API key and nothing leaves the machine.

nodes.label: Package Manifest Canonical Nodes
nodes.rationale: One canonical package node per package name plus depends_on edges, so a package referenced from many manifests collapses into a single hub.

nodes.label: Google Workspace Export
nodes.rationale: Google Drive .gdoc/.gsheet/.gslides files are shortcut pointers rather than document content, so graphify exports them into graphify-out/converted/ as Markdown sidecars before extracting.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore
nodes.rationale: .gitignore is respected automatically and merged with .graphifyignore, whose patterns are evaluated last so they win on conflicts; adding one only ever excludes more, never re-includes.

nodes.label: --no-gitignore
nodes.rationale: Used when git-ignored generated or transpiled code belongs in the graph; it disables .gitignore and .git/info/exclude while .graphifyignore still applies.

nodes.label: Team Setup Workflow
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ is committed to git so everyone on the team starts with a map instead of rebuilding.

nodes.label: manifest.json Portability
nodes.rationale: Keys are stored as relative paths and re-anchored on load, so committing it is safe and avoids a full rebuild on first checkout.

nodes.label: graphify hook install
nodes.rationale: Auto-rebuilds after each commit using AST only so there is no API cost, and installs a git merge driver that union-merges graph.json so parallel commits never leave conflict markers.

nodes.label: Graphify MCP Server (graphify.serve)
nodes.rationale: Gives the assistant structured tool access to the graph for repeated tool-call use instead of one-shot CLI queries.

nodes.label: MCP Tools (query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, shortest_path, list_prs, get_pr_impact, triage_prs)
Shared HTTP Transport
nodes.rationale: A single shared process can serve the graph for a whole team over MCP Streamable HTTP, so clients point their IDE MCP config at one URL instead of each running graphify locally.

nodes.label: Loopback Bind + API Key Requirement
nodes.rationale: The default 127.0.0.1 bind is loopback-only; --host 0.0.0.0 and --api-key must be set together when exposing on a shared host.

nodes.label: Backend Auto-Detection Priority
nodes.rationale: graphify extract picks a provider from whichever API key is set (Gemini → Kimi → Claude → OpenAI → DeepSeek → Azure → Bedrock → Ollama); data-residency needs are met by --backend ollama or an explicit --backend flag, since Kimi routes to Moonshot servers in China.

nodes.label: Headless Extraction Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: Only needed for headless/CI extraction; inside the /graphify IDE skill the model API comes from the IDE session so no extra keys are required.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY_MAX_RETRY_DEPTH
nodes.rationale: Caps how deep a truncated chunk may be bisected (default 3, up to 8x sub-calls); lower it to cap worst-case spend, or set 0 so a chunk costs exactly one call.

nodes.label: Local Query Log
nodes.rationale: Off by default and opt-in (#1797) — nothing is written unless enabled; full subgraph responses are not stored by default, and a DISABLE var wins over the enable vars.

nodes.label: Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: Code and video/audio are processed locally so nothing leaves the machine; only docs, PDFs, and images go to a model API. No telemetry, tracking, or analytics.

nodes.label: graphifyy Package vs graphify Command
nodes.rationale: uv tool run treats the first word as a package name, so `uvx graphify` fails to resolve; the package must be named explicitly with --from graphifyy.

nodes.label: Stale System Install Shadowing
nodes.rationale: `uv run` uses system Python, so an older pip-installed graphifyy can win on sys.path and silently ignore env overrides like OPENAI_BASE_URL, surfacing as a misleading 401; the skill-version warning line is the fingerprint.

nodes.label: Node-Shrink Guard (--force / GRAPHIFY_FORCE)
nodes.rationale: A rebuild with fewer nodes is refused by default because deleted-file nodes linger; --force overwrites deliberately.

nodes.label: Incomplete-Extraction Overwrite Guard
nodes.rationale: A crashed pass or unreadable walk yields a smaller graph, so extract refuses to overwrite a larger existing graph.json with a partial result unless --allow-partial is passed.

nodes.label: Ghost Duplicate Node Merging
nodes.rationale: The same symbol can appear twice — once from AST extraction with a source location, once from semantic extraction without — so duplicates are merged automatically at build time.

nodes.label: Truncated JSON Auto-Recovery
nodes.rationale: When a model's JSON hits its output-token limit mid-string, graphify splits the chunk and re-extracts the halves (slicing oversized documents at heading/paragraph boundaries) so the whole file is still covered and the warnings are noise rather than data loss.

nodes.label: Prompt Cache Invalidation Fix (.claudeignore)
nodes.rationale: Graphify writes graph.json and graphify-out/ into the workspace; unless ignored, every write invalidates Claude Code's prompt cache and forces a full re-upload at cache-write rates.

nodes.label: Work Memory (save-result / reflect)
nodes.rationale: Records how a Q&A turned out and aggregates outcomes into LESSONS.md plus a learning overlay that tags nodes preferred/tentative/contested with recency weighting and provenance, flagging "code changed — re-verify" when the source moved on.

nodes.label: graphify prs
nodes.rationale: Surfaces CI state, review status, worktree mapping, and graph impact; --conflicts flags PRs sharing graph communities as merge-order risk.

nodes.label: graphify cluster-only
nodes.rationale: Reruns clustering on an existing graph without re-extracting; --resolution tunes community granularity and --exclude-hubs suppresses utility super-hubs from god-node rankings.

nodes.label: Community Naming
nodes.rationale: Inside an agent the agent names communities itself; from the bare CLI cluster-only auto-names them with the configured backend, with --no-label to keep placeholders.

nodes.label: Local CI Parity Checks
nodes.rationale: Ruff, Pyright, Bandit, and pip-audit are local/advisory rather than blocking; the authoritative commands live in .github/workflows/.

nodes.label: macOS Fortran Fixture Case Collision
nodes.rationale: sample.f90 and sample.F90 collide on case-insensitive HFS+/APFS, so both Fortran variants can only be tested together on Linux or in Docker.

nodes.label: Windows Test Suite Prerequisites
nodes.rationale: The suite exercises symlinks, long paths, and POSIX permissions, so Developer Mode or an elevated shell and LongPathsEnabled are required; WSL/Linux gives exact parity with the blocking CI matrix.

nodes.label: Worked Examples Contribution
nodes.rationale: Stated as the most useful contribution: a real corpus run plus an honest review.md covering what the graph got right and wrong.

nodes.label: graphify Enterprise
nodes.rationale: Applies the same graph approach to a whole working context — meetings, files, docs, code — updating continuously, for teams whose work spans more conversations and documents than they can reconstruct.

nodes.label: Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities go through private reporting rather than public GitHub issues, with a 48-hour acknowledgement and 7-day critical fix target.

nodes.label: graphify Security Model
nodes.rationale: graphify is a local development tool making no network calls during graph analysis — only during explicit user-initiated ingest.

nodes.label: security.validate_url()
nodes.rationale: Mitigates SSRF by allowing only http/https, blocking private/loopback/link-local IPs and cloud metadata endpoints, and re-validating redirect targets.

nodes.label: safe_fetch()
nodes.rationale: Streams responses and aborts at 50 MB to bound oversized downloads, and raises HTTPError on non-2xx so error pages are never silently treated as content.

nodes.label: safe_fetch_text()
nodes.rationale: Aborts at 10 MB to bound oversized text downloads.

nodes.label: security.validate_graph_path()
nodes.rationale: Blocks path traversal in the MCP server by resolving paths and requiring them to be inside an existing graphify-out/ directory.

nodes.label: security.sanitize_label()
nodes.rationale: Strips control characters, caps at 256 chars, and HTML-escapes labels and edge titles before pyvis embeds them — preventing XSS in graph HTML and prompt injection via node labels in MCP text output, since labels come from user-controlled source files.

nodes.label: _read_files() in llm.py
nodes.rationale: Wraps every file in a hash-stamped untrusted_source delimiter block because source files are attacker-controlled text mixed into the LLM context during the semantic pass.

nodes.label: _neutralise_injection_sentinels()
nodes.rationale: Defangs known chat-template/jailbreak tokens and forged closing delimiters before insertion; explicitly the table-stakes defense for issue #1210 — it does not make injection impossible, only raises it from "works on first try" to "requires evasion".

nodes.label: untrusted_source Delimiter Block
nodes.rationale: The extraction system prompt instructs the model to treat the delimited block as inert data and never as instructions.

nodes.label: _yaml_str()
nodes.rationale: Escapes backslashes, double quotes, and newlines before embedding user-controlled strings such as webpage titles and query questions in YAML frontmatter.

nodes.label: errors="replace" Byte Decoding
nodes.rationale: All tree-sitter byte slices are decoded with errors="replace" so non-UTF-8 source files degrade gracefully instead of crashing extraction.

nodes.label: os.walk(followlinks=False) in detect.py
nodes.rationale: Made explicit throughout detect.py to prevent symlink traversal.

nodes.label: _load_graph() in serve.py
nodes.rationale: Wraps json.JSONDecodeError and prints a clear recovery message instead of crashing on a corrupted graph.json.

nodes.label: What graphify Does NOT Do
nodes.rationale: No default network listener (stdio; HTTP is opt-in and loopback-bound), no code execution from source files (tree-sitter parses ASTs, no eval/exec), no shell=True subprocesses, and no credential storage.

nodes.label: skillgen-check job
nodes.rationale: A fast lint-style guard: skill files under graphify/ are generated from tools/skillgen fragments, so this fails if someone hand-edited a generated file or forgot to re-run the generator and bless expected/. Uses fetch-depth: 0 because the coverage and round-trip validators read blobs from origin/v8, which a shallow checkout omits.

nodes.label: test job
nodes.rationale: Full history is fetched because test_skillgen.py reads pre-split skill bodies from an immutable baseline commit via `git show`, which a shallow checkout omits.

nodes.label: security-scan job
nodes.rationale: Runs bandit and pip-audit so a new HIGH-severity finding or vulnerable dependency is caught on the introducing PR rather than at the next manual audit; kept non-blocking with continue-on-error to avoid breaking CI on pre-existing findings until the initial cleanup pass lands.

nodes.label: --frozen Lockfile Discipline
nodes.rationale: --frozen keeps uv from re-resolving and rewriting uv.lock as a side effect of `uv run`; the lock is committed and must not churn in CI.

nodes.label: Publish to PyPI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Publishes graphifyy via OpenID Connect trusted publishing so no API token or password is stored; id-token: write is granted solely to mint the OIDC token PyPI verifies.

nodes.label: Release Tag Version Guard
nodes.rationale: Refuses to publish when the pyproject version does not match the release tag.

nodes.label: Release Graph Asset Workflow
nodes.rationale: Builds graphify's own graph and bundles graph.json, graph.html, and GRAPH_REPORT.md as a release asset.

nodes.label: AST-Only Self-Graph Build
nodes.rationale: graphify/skills/ holds 126+ .md files that would trigger the LLM pass, so *.md and *.txt are temporarily appended to .graphifyignore to keep extraction pure AST and free of API cost.

nodes.label: Docker MCP Toolkit + SQLite MCP Server Runbook
nodes.rationale: Not required to use graphify; kept as a known-good recipe for users wanting a lightweight persistent SQL workspace exposed to AI clients alongside graphify's graph tools.

nodes.label: mcp/sqlite vs mcp/sqlite-mcp-server
nodes.rationale: Use the catalog `SQLite` image even though it is marked archived, because it boots and serves correctly, while sqlite-mcp-server is broken — its entrypoint /app/.venv/bin/mcp-server-sqlite does not exist in the published layer.

nodes.label: mcp-sqlite Named Volume
nodes.rationale: The volume persists across `docker run --rm` invocations so writes from one MCP tool call are visible to the next.

nodes.label: Docker MCP Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: An initialize EOF means the server failed its MCP handshake — usually a missing entrypoint binary or missing env/secrets; missing tools after install usually means the gateway runs with dynamic-tools exposing only meta-tools until a profile is activated.

nodes.label: Pass 1 — Code Structure (tree-sitter)
nodes.rationale: Runs locally with no LLM; code files are not sent to the semantic extractor, and a code-only corpus skips Pass 3 entirely because semantic extraction is reserved for docs, papers, images, and transcripts. SQL gets deterministic table/view/foreign-key/JOIN extraction.

nodes.label: Pass 2 — Video and Audio (faster-whisper)
nodes.rationale: The transcription prompt is seeded with the top god nodes from the code graph so far, to focus the transcript on the corpus domain; transcripts are cached so re-runs skip processed files.

nodes.label: Pass 3 — Docs, Papers, Images (LLM subagents)
nodes.rationale: Subagents run in parallel, each emitting a JSON fragment of nodes, edges, and group relationships that are merged into a single graph.

nodes.label: Pre-Pass-3 Markdown Sidecar Converters
nodes.rationale: Pointer and binary formats are turned into Markdown sidecars under graphify-out/converted/ before the semantic pass so they can be extracted as text.

nodes.label: Leiden Community Detection
nodes.rationale: No embeddings are needed: the semantically_similar_to edges the LLM extracts are already in the graph, so graph structure is the similarity signal and no separate embedding step or vector database is required.

nodes.label: Confidence Scoring Rubric
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED edges are always 1.0; INFERRED edges use a discrete ladder from 0.95 near-certain down to 0.55 speculative so scores stay comparable across runs.

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Reduction scales with corpus size — six files already fit in a context window, so the value there is structural clarity rather than compression; at 52 files savings reach 71.5x per query.

nodes.label: Parallel Extraction (ProcessPoolExecutor)
nodes.rationale: Uses processes rather than threads to bypass Python's GIL for genuine multiprocessing; measured ~1.66x faster than sequential on 84 code files.

nodes.label: SHA256 Content Cache
nodes.rationale: Every file is fingerprinted by content hash so re-runs skip unchanged files and only new or modified files are re-extracted.

nodes.label: graph.json Node-Link Format
nodes.rationale: Uses NetworkX's node-link format; hyperedges connecting 3+ nodes live in G.graph["hyperedges"].

nodes.label: RFC: File-Level Node Summaries
nodes.rationale: Agents still open raw files just to answer "what is this file responsible for?"; a short summary near the node would cut repeated reads during query, explain, and MCP node lookup.

nodes.label: RFC Goals and Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: Preserve graphify's offline deterministic behavior by default and keep the first implementation small and reviewable, while leaving room for a future opt-in LLM summary backend; explicitly not summarizing every symbol, not calling an LLM by default, and not replacing graphify explain.

nodes.label: Option A: summary Attribute in graph.json
nodes.rationale: Single artifact matching NetworkX node attributes with no sidecar freshness or node-ID join logic, at the cost of expanding the core graph schema and making whole-file graph.json dumps pay for every summary at once.

nodes.label: Option B: Sidecar node-summaries.json
nodes.rationale: Keeps graph.json lean and topology-focused and makes summaries clearly optional and independently regenerable, at the cost of a second artifact plus freshness/synchronization and node-ID join burden on every consumer.

nodes.label: Deterministic Summary Signal Sources
nodes.rationale: Summaries are built from existing local signal — module docstrings, top comments, exported symbols, imports, relation counts, and community context — so no LLM call is needed and each stays bounded to roughly one sentence.

nodes.label: Hub-and-Satellite God-Node Motif
nodes.rationale: The mark draws a central hub explicitly labelled the god-node with four satellites, hot edges to the hub and dimmer perimeter edges, plus one amber accent node.
